newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia stocks fade at close before US data.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia stocks fade at close before US data.

text.p: SPI futures 2343 -17 US 30yr cl 6.64 -0.06
*Stocks ended weaker after a choppy session ahead of a key U.S. labour report. Volume 305.7 million shares, value A$807.9 million, 1,060 stocks traded, 340 steady, 336 up, 384 down

Australian shares finished weaker on Friday ahead of a key U.S. payrolls report later on Friday and after a choppy session which saw the all ordinaries index trade in 20 point range around Thursday's close.
The key All Ordinaries index closed 10.8 points lower at 2,339.4 after touching an intra-day high of 2,357.1.
The December share price index ended down 17 points at 2,343, a slim 3.6 point premium to the underlying index.
Turnover was healthy and aided by see-sawing trade which fed the derivatives market. The market was directionless for much of the session and blue chips were widely mixed, dealers said.
"The gold and bank sectors held the market back for much of the session but there was some good support for some of the big resource issues after lunch," a Sydney-based dealer said.
The dealer said a combination of profit-taking and position squaring dragged stocks lower late in the session, with key resource companies BHP and CRA ending well off intra-day highs.

"Wall Street could go either way tonight, but regardless of this, I think the important focus for the market next week will be local interest rates, especially after the Reserve Bank board meeting next Tuesday and of course the fluctuations of base metal prices on the LME," the dealer said.

Apart from golds, driven lower by a bullion price fall on Thursday, and major banks which were hit by profit-taking, the main interest for the market was the debut of Orogen Minerals, the holding company of Papua New Guinea's Mineral Resources Development Corp.
After getting off to a slow start, Orogen finished the day at A$2.12, a six percent premium to the stocks institutional offer price of A$2.00.
In other markets, Australian bonds ended little changed in cautious trade ahead of U.S. jobs data despite weak local retail data which was seen as raising hopes for a local rate cut.
The yield on 10-year T-bonds closed at 7.41 percent, up 0.01 percentage points from Thursday's closing level.
The Australian dollar began to show the wear and tear of weeks of rate cut speculation, especially after the release of weak September retail trade data.
At 5.00 p.m. (0600 GMT), the unit was quoted at US$0.7898/03.
FUTURES/OPTIONS - Options trade was steady while futures business was lifted by the market's intra-session volatility.
Total options traded 37,729 (37,174)
